name: Payload Fairing Halves
summary: Reusable two-piece 5.2 m composite clamshell enclosing the satellite payload during atmospheric ascent.
function: Protects payloads from aerodynamic pressure, acoustic vibration, and aero-heating through the dense atmosphere, then separates pneumatically above ~115 km for recovery at sea.
materials: Carbon-fiber composite skins bonded over an aluminum honeycomb core with internal acoustic foam blankets.
history: Valued at roughly $6M per pair, SpaceX developed cold-gas steering and steerable parafoils to recover and re-fly fairing halves from the ocean surface.
